name: matcher plain SQL before comma
why: Spec: plain strings match case-insensitively and the character after the term must not be a letter, digit, underscore, "&", "+" or "/"; a comma is allowed.

name: matcher SQL inside NoSQL
why: Spec: the character before the term must not be a letter, digit, underscore, "&", "+" or "/". In "NoSQL" the character before S is the letter o.

name: matcher SQL prefix of SQLite
why: Spec: the character after the term must not be a letter, digit, underscore, "&", "+" or "/". In "SQLite" the character after L is the letter i.

name: matcher case-sensitive R whole token
why: Spec: {"t":"R","cs":true} matches only with exact case; the example says it matches "Python or R.".

name: matcher case-sensitive R does not match lowercase r
why: Spec: "cs": true terms match only with the exact case.

name: matcher case-sensitive R before ampersand
why: Spec: the character after the term must not be "&"; the example says {"t":"R","cs":true} does not match "R&D".

name: matcher ML inside HTML
why: Spec: the character before the term must not be a letter; the example says "ML" does not match "HTML". In "HTML" the character before M is T.

name: matcher term with internal slash
why: Spec: "A/B testing" matches "A/B testing" (the slash is inside the term); boundary before is a space and after is a space.

name: split_req no marker
why: Spec: no marker means (whole text, "").

name: split_req nice to have marker
why: Spec: split at the first occurrence of "nice to have"; required part is everything before that word, preferred part is from that word to the end.
text: Required: Python. Nice to have: SQL

name: split_req case-insensitive bonus
why: Spec: markers are matched case-insensitively; split at the first occurrence of "bonus".

name: split_req first marker wins
why: Spec: the text is split at the FIRST occurrence of any marker; required part is before "Bonus", preferred part starts at "Bonus".
text: Python and SQL. Bonus: Docker. Nice to have: AWS
expect_preferred: Bonus: Docker. Nice to have: AWS

name: split_req hyphenated nice-to-have
why: Spec: "nice-to-have" is one of the whole-word markers; split before it and keep it in the preferred part.

name: stats single hit required
why: One JD with SQL in the required part: keyword df=1/1=1.000, req_share=1/1=1.0; competency df=1, req_share=1, score=1*(0.5+0.5*1)=1, weight=1/1=1.0000.

name: stats keyword df rounded and required-only hits
why: SQL hits 2 of 3 JDs, so keyword df=2/3=0.666… rounded to 0.667; both SQL hits are in required parts, so req_share=1.0; competency hits 2/3 JDs, all required, score≈0.6667, weight=1.0000 as only competency.

name: stats hit only in preferred part
why: The only SQL hit is after the "Bonus" marker, so keyword df=1/1=1.000 but req_share=0/1=0.0; competency df=1, req_share=0, score=1*(0.5+0)=0.5, weight=1.0000 as only competency.

name: stats competency union over groups
why: Python hits JDs 1 and 2 (df=2/3=0.667), SQL hits JDs 1 and 3 (df=2/3=0.667); their union hits all 3 JDs, so competency df=1.0; all hits are required, so req_share=1.0; score=1, weight=1.0000.

name: stats two competencies weights
why: Python hits 4/4 JDs: df=1, req_share=1, score=1. SQL hits 2/4 JDs: df=0.5, req_share=1, score=0.5. Sum=1.5, so Python weight=1/1.5=0.6667 and SQL weight=0.5/1.5=0.3333; descending order is py then sql.

name: stats req_share affects score
why: SQL hits both JDs anywhere (df=2/2=1.000), but only JD1 has SQL in the required part; req_share=1/2=0.5, score=1*(0.5+0.5*0.5)=0.75, weight=1.0000 as only competency.

name: stats no hits gives zero weights
why: SQL never hits the only JD, so keyword df=0.000 and req_share=0.0; competency df=0, score=0, and when every score is 0 every weight is 0.

name: stats df below 0.05 gives score zero
why: SQL hits 1 of 21 JDs: 1/21=0.047619, rounded keyword df=0.048, still below 0.05; competency df≈0.0476<0.05, so score=0 and weight=0.0000 when all scores are zero.

name: select basic track and sorting
why: Spec: chosen when its track is in selector.tracks and it has a text and no truthy dup_of; result ids are unique and sorted ascending.

name: select excludes missing text and truthy dup_of
why: Spec: a job is chosen only if its id has a text and it has no (truthy) dup_of. b has no text; c has truthy dup_of; d has falsy dup_of "" so it is allowed.

name: select title_regex case-insensitive
why: Spec: if selector has title_regex, a chosen job must also match it in its title (case-insensitive). Only a and c have Python in the title.

name: select or_tracks_with_text min_hits
why: Spec: OR, when or_tracks_with_text is given, a job is chosen if its track is in those tracks AND the regex matches at least min_hits times. a has 3 SQL matches, c has 2, b has 1; d is included by selector.tracks.

name: select regex non-overlapping matches
why: Spec: regex matches are non-overlapping. In "ababa" the regex "aba" gives 1 match; in "abaaba" it gives 2 matches, so only b reaches min_hits=2.

name: select combines title_regex with or_tracks_with_text
why: Spec: a chosen job must also satisfy title_regex. a qualifies via or_tracks_with_text (data track, two Python matches) and title matches Engineer; b fails title; c qualifies via tracks and title; d fails title; e has no text.
